correctness.rationale: For K3□Kn, pairwise distance≤2 makes a triple illegal exactly when the selected K_{3,n} edges contain a three-edge path. Legal states are bipartite star forests. All maximal states have 3,n,n+1 edges. Two-in-one-row play has high locks at a column pair plus third-row edge (n+1) and middle locks with three occupied distinct columns (n). Responding to off-row deviations and who moves at n−1 filled columns gives the parity outcome for each opening player. Independent exact minimax recurrence over all legal selected subsets for n=3,4,5,6 gives (4,3),(4,5),(6,5),(6,7) matching formulas; infinite proof is the exhaustive strategic case reasoning.

value.rationale: Adversarial general-position games ask for forced terminal sizes rather than static extremal sizes. The natural narrow family K3□Kn has a complete parity-reversing optimal-play classification, with explicit high and middle locking strategies, a structural behavioral distinction not mechanically inferable from known maximal-set cardinalities.
